title: Permission Guardrails and SIEM Shuttle Spec
content:
Purpose and scope

This working spec defines permission guardrails (RBAC v2), a compact audit payload schema, and the behaviour of the "SIEM shuttle" — the lightweight export/transform agent we use to deliver evidence to customer SIEMs and our internal analytics pipeline. It is intended to support three hosting modes: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.

Goals
- Provide a crisp role matrix aligned to customer-facing personas (platform admin, tenant admin, tenant operator, telemetry reader).
- Define minimal policy templates (JSON policy snippets) customers can apply for each hosting mode.
- Standardize an audit payload that balances fidelity and PII minimization for SIEM export.
- Describe evidence automation flows (how evidence bundles are assembled and verified for audits).
- Document how the SIEM shuttle transforms and ships data by environment with explicit configuration knobs for retention, PII redaction and signing.

Design principles
- Least privilege focused: default-deny for admin operations; explicit allow lists.
- Environment-aware policies: tighter defaults for Hosted, explicit tenant separation for Dedicated, and local-operator-first for Private.
- Audit-first: every sensitive action emits a single canonical audit event and a corresponding evidence artifact when required.
- Composable templates: short policy snippets that can be combined rather than monolithic role definitions.

High-level role matrix (concise)
Columns: role | primary intent | typical principals | allowed scopes | typical operations
- Platform-Org-Admin | manage Redwood account and org-level config | security team, SRE | org* | create/modify environments, billing, platform-wide keys
- Hosting-Tier-Admin | manage Hosted/Dedicated/Private infra configs | infra eng, platform ops | hosting-tier* | manage capacity pools, fallback policies, kms linking
- Tenant-Admin | customer tenant owner | customer IT | tenant:* | create API keys, configure tenant policies, view billing usage
- Tenant-Operator | application deployer for a tenant | devops/engineers | tenant:app* | deploy model routes, set rollout policies, restart workers
- Telemetry-Reader | read-only telemetry access | security analysts, SOC | telemetry:* | read logs, request traces, cost/latency dashboards
- Support-ShortLived | temporary troubleshooting rights | support staff | scoped-timebound | view logs, reproduce requests (redacted), create incident notes

Notes:
- "*" denotes wildcard scoping that must be constrained by policy assignment.
- Timebound roles (Support-ShortLived) must be requested via privilege activation (MFA + ticket) and automatically revoked.

Policy templates (snippets, illustrative not exhaustive)
1) Minimal tenant admin (Hosted):
{
  "effect": "allow",
  "action": ["tenant.keys.create", "tenant.keys.list", "tenant.config.update"],
  "resource": ["arn:redwood:tenant:${TENANT_ID}:*"]
}

2) Dedicated capacity operator (example):
{
  "effect": "allow",
  "action": ["dedicated.pool.allocate", "dedicated.pool.resize", "dedicated.node.reboot"],
  "resource": ["arn:redwood:dedicated:${POOL_ID}:*"]
}

3) Read-only telemetry (redacted PII):
{
  "effect": "allow",
  "action": ["telemetry.query", "telemetry.trace.read"],
  "condition": {"redaction": "pii_high"},
  "resource": ["arn:redwood:telemetry:${ORG_ID}:*"]
}

Policy assignment and enforcement
- All policy checks are evaluated at control plane gateway for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments we ship an enforcement agent that uses the same evaluation library but runs locally (signed policy bundles).
- Policy bindings must include: principal identifier, scope, assignment-issue timestamp, TTL (for timebound roles) and source (ui|api|manual-onboard).

Audit payload schema (canonical event)
Every sensitive operation emits an audit event with the following canonical fields (flat schema):
- event_id: string (UUID)
- timestamp_utc: string (ISO8601)
- principal_id: string (opaque id)
- principal_type: string (user|service|support-bot)
- action: string (e.g., "tenant.api_key.create")
- resource_arn: string (ARN-style resource)
- env_mode: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- outcome: string (success|failure|denied)
- request_context: string (short text: remote_ip, region, user_agent)
- policy_version: string (rbac-v2-YYYYMM)
- evidence_refs: string (comma-separated evidence artifact ids)
- redaction_level: string (none|pii_low|pii_high)
- request_id: string (trace id)

Schema rationale and PII handling
- principal_id is an opaque id inside RBAC v2; PIIs like email are only present when redaction_level==none and only in evidence artifacts, not the canonical event.
- request_context is a short field intended for routing; detailed request bodies (prompts, examples) go into evidence artifacts with their own storage/retention rules.

Evidence artifact conventions
- Types: config-snapshot, request-dump (redacted), keystore-audit, rollout-diff, access-evidence (privilege activation logs).
- Naming: evidence-YYYYMMDD-<event_id>-<type>.tar.gz (stored in GCS/S3)
- Integrity: every artifact must be SHA256-signed and a signed manifest entry is recorded in the audit event's evidence_refs.

Evidence automation runbook (high-level)
Steps:
1) Trigger: audit event emitted for sensitive operation or periodic evidence collection job.
2) Collector: short-lived pod collects relevant artifacts (config snapshot, logs matching trace id, minimal request payloads) and applies redaction policy.
3) Sign + store: artifact compressed, signed by KMS (org or customer KMS depending on environment), uploaded to evidence bucket.
4) Link: collector returns evidence id(s) to control plane; control plane writes evidence_refs into canonical event.
5) Verify: scheduled verifier compares manifest signatures and ensures artifact TTL complies with retention policy for environment.

Environment differences (hosted | dedicated | private)
Hosted:
- Default: Redwood-managed KMS for artifact signing, 90d retention for request-dumps, longer for config snapshots (365d).
- Tenant data is logically partitioned; additional PII redaction defaults to pii_high for external support roles.
- SIEM Shuttle runs in a managed tenant-export pool with tenant consent mapping (customers opt into delivery endpoints).

Dedicated:
- Customer-owned pools; we offer two modes: 
  a) Centralized export: Redwood SIEM shuttle collects and ships to customer SIEM (requires customer-approved export contract).
  b) Local export: customer runs the shuttle in their VPC; artifacts signed with customer KMS.
- Retention and redaction defaults are negotiated in contract; default: 180d for request-dumps.

Private:
- No offsite export by default. SIEM shuttle is shipped as a vetted binary/helm chart that runs locally.
- Evidence signing must use customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Support access requires customer granting timebound roles and generating an access ticket; we recommend support playbooks that produce evidence bundles before any privileged session.

SIEM shuttle behaviour and transform rules
- Input: event stream (canonical events) + artifacts references.
- Transform pipeline steps: 
  1) Enrich: add region, cluster-id, tenant alias.
  2) Redact: apply redaction_level from event (pii_high removes prompt text, user-provided metadata; pii_low removes emails/ssns but keeps non-sensitive text).
  3) Fingerprint: compute activity fingerprint for dedupe across retries.
  4) Sign: add shuttle signature header (shuttle_id + signature).
  5) Ship: push to configured endpoint (syslog over TLS, HTTPS with mutual TLS, or S3/GCS ingestion).

Configuration knobs (shuttle config keys)
- ship.mode = [syslog|https|s3]
- redaction.default = [pii_high|pii_low|none]
- retention.override_days = integer (maximum retention to request from downstream)
- signing.kms = [redwood|customer-kms:arn]
- include.artifacts = [config-snapshot,request-dump,keystore-audit]

Operational playbook (example use cases)
Case A: SOC alert (Hosted)\- SOC triggers investigation -> Telemetry-reader accesses traces (redacted) -> Support-ShortLived requested for tenant -> evidence collector creates request-dump with pii_low -> shuttle ships event+artifact to SOC SIEM endpoint.

Case B: Customer audit (Dedicated, customer-hosted shuttle)\- Customer requests artifact bundle -> agent collects config snapshot + signed keystore-audit -> artifacts signed with customer KMS -> admin downloads bundle via signed URL with short TTL.

Developer notes / implementation TODOs
- Finalize RBAC binding fields and canonical principal schema (RFC by eng-security).
- Add sample policy generator tool to produce ARNs and TTLs for timebound roles.
- Integrate shuttle with log-token rotation (rotate signing keys quarterly).
- Bake-in tests: redaction property-based tests and round-trip signature verification.

Open questions
- Should we permit raw prompt text in Hosted events for anonymized internal analytics? (privacy/legal tradeoff)
- What SLA will we guarantee for artifact retrieval in Dedicated mode (RTO targets)?
- Should evidence_refs be an array in the canonical event (we store as comma-list currently for payload simplicity)?

Appendix: quick checklist for onboarding a new tenant (security ops)
- Confirm tenant admin principal created + MFA enforced.
- Assign Tenant-Admin and Telemetry-Reader roles (least privilege).
- Configure retention defaults (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Verify shuttle endpoint is configured and test a signed event + artifact flow.
- Run verifier job and confirm SHA256 manifests match.

End of spec (working draft)

Notes to self: convert this doc into a Confluence RFC, add diagrams for shuttle pipeline and role assignment flow.
